name: Guaraní
notes: Paraguayan Guaraní (avañe'ẽ), co-official language of Paraguay, written in the achegety. Six oral vowels /a e i o u ɨ/ and a nasal counterpart for each, written with a tilde ⟨ã ẽ ĩ õ ũ ỹ⟩; ⟨y⟩ is the close central unrounded vowel /ɨ/, not a glide, and the palatal obstruent /dʒ~ʝ/ is written ⟨j⟩. The acute accent ⟨á é í ó ú ý⟩ marks lexical stress and has no segmental value. Consonants: the plosives /p t k/ and the glottal stop /ʔ/, written ⟨'⟩ and called the puso; the fricatives /s ʃ h/ written ⟨s ch h⟩; the nasals /m n ɲ/ written ⟨m n ñ⟩; the tap /ɾ/ written ⟨r⟩ and the retroflex of Spanish loans written ⟨rr⟩; the approximants /ʋ ɰ l/ written ⟨v g l⟩; and the nasal-oral contour stops ⟨mb nd ng nt⟩. ⟨g̃⟩ is the nasal counterpart of ⟨g⟩ /ɰ/, written as a base ⟨g⟩ plus U+0303 COMBINING TILDE. The letters ⟨b c d⟩ are not letters of the achegety on their own and never occur bare: across both gold sets every ⟨b⟩ falls inside ⟨mb⟩, every ⟨c⟩ inside ⟨ch⟩ and every ⟨d⟩ inside ⟨nd⟩, with no bare token of any of the three. The nasal-oral stops are in complementary distribution with the plain nasals: a plain nasal surfaces before a nasal vowel and the contour stop before an oral vowel. The orthography follows that distribution, so ⟨mb nd ng⟩ are written only before oral vowels — all 89 tokens of the three digraphs in the wikipron gold are, and none before a nasal vowel — and the contour stop is therefore the right first reading. The plain nasal is carried as a second reading because it is the loose transcription of the same phone: the wikipron gold writes plain [m] for ⟨mb⟩ in 33 of 50 words and [ᵐb] in 17, [n] for ⟨nd⟩ in 20 of 28 and [ⁿd] in 8, [ŋ] for ⟨ng⟩ in 6 of 11 and [ᵑɡ] in 4. That is a transcription convention rather than a second phone — the gold drops the oral release outright rather than hearing a second one (kamba is transcribed k a m a, mbo'e as m o ʔ e, while the sister form kamby with an oral vowel keeps it: k a m b ɨ) — so the ranking is not flipped to chase it; keeping the reading in the lattice moves oracle@5 on wikipron from 0.1347 to 0.0819. Nasal harmony, the language's most distinctive process, spreads leftward from a nasal vowel in a stressed syllable across the whole word, nasalising the vowels it passes and the sonorants among them while voiceless obstruents stay transparent. It is described here but not modelled: the rule layer has no directional word-scope predicate and can only express the process's final local step — a vowel nasalising immediately before a nasal vowel — never the leftward chain across the rest of the word, and the wikipron gold does not record harmony in any of the eight words that step alone would touch (heẽ, kuñataĩ, kuñataĩnguéra, leõ, peteĩ, peẽ, peẽme, poteĩ): it contradicts the local rule in all eight. The gold is not even consistent with its own practice here — kuñataĩ is transcribed k ũ ɲ ã t a ĩ, nasalising ũ and ã from ⟨ñ⟩ while leaving the a before ĩ oral, the very hiatus the rule would nasalise. So no harmony rule is shipped rather than a wrongly-shaped one. Modelling the process properly needs a leftward word-scope predicate in the engine.

sources.author: Cabrera Sanchez, Marisabel
sources.title: Nasal harmony in Paraguayan Guarani: Positional effects and the representation of nasality
sources.publisher: University of California, Los Angeles (MA thesis)
sources.notes: Consulted. The consonant chart on p. 11 gives the phones with their achegety spellings: plosives p t k ʔ ⟨'⟩; nasal-oral stops mb ⟨mb⟩, nd ⟨nd⟩, ŋg ⟨ng⟩; nasals m, n, ɲ ⟨ñ⟩, ŋ ⟨g̃⟩; fricatives s, ʃ ⟨ch⟩, ʤ ⟨j⟩, h; approximants ʋ ⟨v⟩, ɾ ⟨r⟩, ɰ ⟨g⟩. The same page names ⟨'⟩ the puso and gives it the value [ʔ]. Page 12 states that the velar consonants [ŋg] ⟨ng⟩, [ɰ] ⟨g⟩ and [ŋ] ⟨g̃⟩ occur infrequently and are overwhelmingly labialized, and that 'Stress is predominantly word final, although a limited number of forms show penultimate stress'. Page 14 states that regressive nasal spread is triggered by nasal vowels in stressed syllables and nasalises all vowels to the left as well as sonorant consonants, with voiceless stops and fricatives transparent, and on the same page states that the nasal-oral stops are in complementary distribution with the plain nasals: 'nasal consonants emerge when followed by a nasal vowel, and nasal-oral stops emerge when followed by an oral vowel'.

orthography_standard.name: Achegety
orthography_standard.notes: The 33-letter Guaraní alphabet: the twelve vowels, the simple consonants, the digraphs ⟨ch mb nd ng nt rr⟩, the tilde letters ⟨ñ g̃⟩ and the puso ⟨'⟩. The puso is written with U+0027 APOSTROPHE in both gold sets scored here (998 tokens in vox_communis, 68 in wikipron, and no U+2019 or U+02BC token in either), so that is the codepoint keyed. ⟨g̃⟩ is likewise a base ⟨g⟩ plus U+0303 COMBINING TILDE rather than a precomposed character, which has no precomposed form in Unicode.

stress.notes: Stress is word-final by default; the acute accent marks a lexically stressed vowel elsewhere and has no segmental value. ⟨y⟩ is a vowel letter in Guaraní, and is declared here so the syllabifier does not read it as the glide the cross-linguistic shape test would make it.
